DR. DINNO T. DEPOSITARIO Assistant Department Head/HRMO Head Designate Office of City Human Resource Dumaguete City Dear Dr. Depositario: This pertains to your letter dated 30 July 2018 to Dir. Dennis Quinones, Provincial Director, DILG Negros Oriental requesting for legal opinion on whether the SK Chairman can possibly be hired as Job Order (JO) Employee of Dumaguete City. Relative thereto, may we invite you to Section 94 (a) of the Local Government Code (LGC) which provides: "(a) No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. " It is clear based on above-cited provision of the LGC that an elective or appointive local official is not allowed to hold in any capacity other office in the Government, its subdivision, agency or instrumentality, including GOCC. However, grounded on the query at hand, we should also answer if the said official can be hired as JO or Contract of Services (COS) employees of any of the government offices, like the City of Dumaguete. In relation thereto, on point is our affirmation that Sangguniang Kabataan Officials are within the purview Of the term "local elective officials" and they are covered by the prohibition under Section 94 (a) of the LGC. In view of the foregoing, it is our opinion that the law intended the public officials not to hold any position in the government in whatever capacity, unless specifically allowed by law. Page 1 of2 S. 2018

On the other hand, even if it was established that JO and COS has no employer- employee (EE-ER) relationship with the government, being a JO or COS in the government is still an "employment in the government" or he is considered "holding a public office': Therefore, we find the herein principle applicable, viz: " What cannot be legally done directly cannot be done indirectly. This rule is basic and, to a reasonable mind, does not need explanation. Indeed, if acts that cannot be legally done directly can be done indirectly, then all laws would be illusory. " In other words, since elective officials are proscribed to be employed in the government during their tenure, they should not be allowed to circumvent the law by hiring them in the guise Of JO or COS, because it will make this proscription useless, and will result in doing indirectly what is not legal. Hence, it is this Department's position that elective or appointive local officials cannot be hired as JO or COS employee in any government office or GOCC. Lastly, please be informed however, that SK Officials are allowed to accept employment in private offices or practice their profession as long as it does not conflict with his/her duties in the SK. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ITYOFTH CRETARY: TIN B DINO U ndersecretary Copy furnished: Dir. Leocadio T.
